subject: Service evacuation notice — immediate regional traffic reshuffle and short-term guidance
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ari Jacobs <ari.jacobs@examplecorp.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Dec 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Service evacuation notice — immediate regional traffic reshuffle and short-term guidance

Ari / Samantha —

Quick heads up: we're seeing a progressive networking degradation in EU West and APAC-Sydney cloud hubs impacting inference traffic that originates from those POPs. Root cause analysis is ongoing, but our telemetry shows increased packet loss between our edge ingress and the region gateways leading to request timeouts and elevated latency for customers pinned to those regions.

Immediate mitigation we are activating now (what you can expect):
- We will temporarily shift customer traffic away from EU West and APAC-Sydney to adjacent regions (EU Central and US East) using a traffic reshuffle lane. This will preserve throughput but may increase RTT for some requests.
- For customers using the SDK or service tokens with region affinity, set region preference to "us-east-1" or "eu-central-1" until we confirm recovery. Example SDK flag: region_preference="us-east-1".
- Prefix caching is preserved during the switch; there should be no loss of conversational context.

Ask for you:
1) Can you toggle any client-side regional pinning for test accounts for the next 4–8 hours?
2) If you see elevated error rates after the switch, send traces to support@redwood.com with header X-Redwood-Trace.

Attachments: incident_region_map.png (map of impacted POPs) — quick routing commands in routing_fix_commands.txt are coming in a follow-up.

I'll keep you posted as we roll the temporary routing rules. Expected update 60–90 minutes.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0193

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Dec 2028 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service evacuation notice — immediate regional traffic reshuffle and short-term guidance

Thanks Ben —

Ops update (internal TL;DR):
- Networking vendor reported an upstream peering flap affecting two EU and one APAC backbone hop. Our control plane is healthy.
- We're applying a routing policy in the edge router group to steer traffic to eu-central-1 and us-east-1. This is an automated traffic-level policy (no customer config required) for the next 3 hours, then we'll reassess.
- Can send a one-click SDK snippet for customers who prefer an explicit override. Laura, I'll hand you the snippet to include in the customer note.

I'll post the incident timeline and a copy of the routing commands to the Drive folder referenced.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ari Jacobs <ari.jacobs@examplecorp.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@brightretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Dec 2028 09:50:00 -0800
Subject: Customer guidance — short term routing change and recommended SDK flag

Ari / Samantha —

Following up with the concrete steps to minimize user impact. We'll be moving traffic away from EU West and APAC-Sydney to neighboring regions while the upstream provider resolves the peering instability. Recommended short-term actions if you want to proactively pin clients:

1) SDK override (recommended for test envs):
   - Node/python: set clientOptions.region_preference = "us-east-1"
   - HTTP: add X-Redwood-Region: us-east-1

2) For production traffic: rely on our temporary routing policy — we do not recommend wide client-side pinning unless you're validating behavior.

3) Expected impact: +80–150ms median latency for affected requests; error rate should drop after the shift.

Attachment: routing_fix_commands.txt (CLI and cURL examples). Please reply with any questions or if you want us to run the override on specific service tokens.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Ari Jacobs <ari.jacobs@examplecorp.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Dec 2028 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Customer guidance — short term routing change and recommended SDK flag

Thanks Laura / Ben —

We saw a spike in 504s this morning around 09:05 PT. We toggled our retry window for reads to 2s and reduced concurrency, which helped in a test cluster. Please go ahead and apply the temporary routing change for our production tokens; we'd prefer Redwood to manage the switch centrally.

Could you also confirm how long session affinity / KV cache validity will be preserved after the shift? We run streaming sessions for conversational agents and are worried about the cache TTL.

— Ari
Ari Jacobs
Platform Ops, ExampleCorp
ari.jacobs@examplecorp.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ari Jacobs <ari.jacobs@examplecorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Dec 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Customer guidance — short term routing change and recommended SDK flag

Ari —

We will execute the central traffic shift for your production tokens at 11:15 PT. Quick answers:
- KV cache: intact. We replicate KV cache state when we fail traffic between compatible region variants for short-duration moves (<6 hours). For longer moves there is a warmup period (~2–5 minutes) where you may see slightly higher token generation times as cache rehydrates.
- Streaming sessions: we will maintain TCP/TLS session continuity where possible; for clients that open new connections, we recommend allowing a 10–20s reconnect window.
- We'll include a short window where we accept both old and new region endpoints to minimize cutover errors.

I'll send a confirmation when the routing policy is live and include a short timeline file in the Drive link.

— Monica

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ari Jacobs <ari.jacobs@examplecorp.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@brightretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 08 Dec 2028 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Service evacuation notice — post-incident follow-up and next steps

Ari / Samantha —

Final note: routing shift completed at 11:17 PT yesterday. Our post-change metrics show error rates for your tokens dropped to baseline within 4 minutes and median latency stabilized at +95ms compared to your normal EU West baseline. The upstream provider has confirmed partial restoration; we'll keep eu-west routing in a guarded state until they fully validate peering stability (ETA 12–24 hours).

Next steps:
- We're scheduling a postmortem and will include a summary of timelines, root cause, and remediation items by EOD Monday.
- If you want a joint ops call to walk the timeline and mitigation details, we can set something up early next week.

Thanks for the quick coordination here — appreciate the patience.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
